key_insight: Giving research agents more time, more parallel workers, or opportunities to collaborate eventually produces diminishing returns as their histories accumulate. The paper points to forgetting as a potential ingredient for sustained discovery, although the supplied abstract is incomplete.
problem_solved: How to keep automated research productive when additional computation and agent collaboration no longer yield continued improvements.
method: Use LLM agents to iteratively refine research candidates with feedback from scored verifiers.
Compare three scaling strategies: longer individual runs, independent parallel agents, and parallel agents that share and build on candidates.
Examine performance plateaus associated with accumulated history; the excerpt does not specify the forgetting mechanism or detailed results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, simply increasing agent runtime or team size may not sustain progress. History management and selective forgetting are worth investigating alongside compute scaling.
visual_elements: Three-panel diagram comparing longer runs, parallel agents, and communicating agent teams.
Conceptual discovery-progress curves that flatten as research continues, clearly labeled as illustrative.
Agent memory timeline showing accumulated history and a potential selective-forgetting step.
Feedback-loop diagram connecting candidate generation, verifier scoring, and refinement.
paper_authors: Shangyin Tan, Ben Zhou, Lakshya A Agrawal, Jialin Zhang, Yilin Chen
